evidence: src/domain/types.ts: OrderStateTransitions is the only state-transition table; OrderDomainService.canTransition reads it, and validateTransition calls canTransition instead of repeating the check

src/domain/errors.ts: InsufficientStockError, InvalidStateTransitionError, OrderNotFoundError and ProductNotFoundError all extend DomainError; order-service.ts throws these classes rather than plain Error
src/domain/repositories.ts: ProductRepository and OrderRepository are typed only in terms of Product, Order and OrderState from types.ts

src/domain/order-service.ts: OrderDomainService keeps reservations in a private Map<string, StockReservation[]> rather than a repository; this is a design weakness but not a split or duplicated invariant

src/domain/order-service.ts: canTransition(fromState: OrderState, toState: string) casts toState to OrderState, and reserveStock always passes available=0 to InsufficientStockError; both are minor typing/accuracy issues, not cohesion breaks
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The src/domain module covers one cohesive concern, the order/product domain. types.ts defines the model (Order, OrderItem, Product, StockReservation, OrderState) and the single transition table, OrderStateTransitions. errors.ts defines a DomainError hierarchy. repositories.ts declares persistence ports typed only in terms of types.ts. order-service.ts holds the order state-transition and stock-reservation logic. The transition invariant lives in one place: canTransition reads OrderStateTransitions, and validateTransition calls canTransition instead of repeating the check. The service throws the module's own error classes rather than plain Error. Three minor weak spots do not amount to a split or duplication: (1) OrderDomainService keeps reservation state in a private in-memory Map instead of a repository, so reservations only survive if one shared service instance is used; this is the closest thing to bypassing the module's abstractions and is why confidence is moderate. (2) canTransition and validateTransition take toState as a plain string and cast it to OrderState. (3) InsufficientStockError is always given available=0.
